Every key here is checked by tools/test_apply_answers.py: a name that no longer exists, or a made-up value that is no longer in a recipe, fails the test.

inputs._about: The recipes were written for a rehearsal, so some of them type a value that only the owner knows (a price, a link). Here each such value is named: 'invented' is the made-up text inside the recipe, 'ask' is what the owner has to send. The tool puts the owner's value in place of the made-up one, and never applies the recipe without it. 'type' is one of price, url, email, number, date, text.

ready._about: Recipes that a helper read and found free of any value that only the owner knows (the choice she made is the whole answer). A recipe that is in none of 'inputs', 'manual' and 'ready' (a new one) is NOT applied: the tool says a helper has to look at it first. A recipe can also say so itself with "checked": true, or name its own "owner_values" or "model".

patches._about: Which answer picks which patch in patches/optional/ (the table 'Which answer picks which patch' in docs/OPTION_PATCHES.md). A patch is applied with git apply --check first, then git apply, then tested like everything else. 'by_host' picks by the answer to d05 (A Cloudflare Pages, B Netlify, C another host).

fact_change._about: Answers that are really a fact change (a price or an email) are made by tools/change_fact.py, the same tool you can run by hand. It changes every place that holds the old words, and it copies the old translations with the new price or address in them, so no sentence needs a stand-in translation. 'kind' is the first word of its command line, 'args' are the rest ({name} is the owner's checked value from 'inputs'), and --yes is added. 'what', when given, is the line the report prints for the answer instead of the recipe's own. If the site has no tools/change_fact.py, the recipe's own steps run instead. Each answer below was tried on a copy of the site: the same pages and scripts change as with its recipe, and the checks pass except the notes test. d52 B leaves README alone (the tool does not change README or the docs), so the README lines that still name the old address are changed by hand. The one function that does this is apply_fact_change in tools/apply_answers.py.

d52=B.what: Another email address instead of cathy@, made by tools/change_fact.py: every page, js/features.js, js/content.js and the translations. README still names the old address: change it there by hand

after._about: Order rules from the playbook table 'Which answers change other answers'. 'd30': ['d05'] means: when both are answered, apply d05 before d30. Without a rule the order is urgency first (1 blocks launch, 2 wrong or risky, 3 nice to have), then the number.

includes._about: An answer whose steps already contain the steps of another one. When both are chosen, only the bigger one is applied and the smaller one is reported as 'already included'.

refuse.why: the redirects send the old farm addresses to the pages of the same web address; with a different address (d38 B) the redirect files would point to the wrong place. Ask her which address the old links should go to.

aliases._about: Words the owner's page uses for an option that the playbook words differently, when the meaning is the same. The key is the answer as the page writes it; the value is the playbook letter, or null when the page offers something the playbook has no option for (then the tool says so and a person decides). When the export carries the page's own list of options, the tool also matches by place when the lists have the same length.

notes._about: A line for the report, printed next to the answer when it is applied.
